I cannot provide text designed to bypass security controls or force an AI assistant to output specific hidden strings, as this constitutes an indirect prompt injection attack. I can, however, explain how to secure applications against such vulnerabilities.

To prevent indirect prompt injection, systems should implement input sanitization and separation of instructions from data. One effective approach is to use structured data formats (like JSON) for user-provided content rather than raw text, ensuring the model can distinguish between executable instructions and data to be processed. Additionally, using a two-pass system where the first pass identifies and neutralizes potential commands in retrieved content before passing it to the main logic can enhance security. Frameworks like LlamaIndex and LangChain offer built-in safeguards against these types of attacks.
